fixes.correction: Make this a TIGHT CLOSE-UP INSERT, not a figure shot. The frame is filled by one single unbound palm-leaf strip lying flat and open on a dark wooden low writing desk, seen from slightly above. Across its surface run five or six short horizontal rows of fine, dark, scratched incised strokes, abstract marks only, with no legible letters, no script-like glyphs and no numerals. Ramayyan's thin, brown right hand enters from the top edge, with only the hand, the wrist and the edge of a plain white cotton cloth showing. It holds a slim iron stylus whose point HOVERS a finger's width above one row, clearly lifted and stopped, NOT touching the leaf. No face, no head, no other people, no doorway, no courtyard. Use warm, low light from a small brass oil lamp with an open wick just out of frame, and keep the same dark wood desk and woven mat as the war-hall anteroom. Leave a plain, low-detail band of dark desk surface along the bottom quarter of the frame, clear of the hand and the stylus point, for two captions.
fixes.issues: v01 is not acceptable. 1) Framing: the script asks for a tight insert of a leaf and a stylus, but v01 is a medium shot of the whole figure with two extra turbaned men in a doorway, and it duplicates the 2.1 setup. 2) Action: the stylus point is pressed into the leaf as if writing, not held still above one name. No list of names shows, only the edge of a closed bundle. 3) Likeness: this Ramayyan has a grey moustache and slicked-back grey hair. The sheet shows him clean-shaven with curly black hair around a receding crown. In this form he would merge with Mathoo Tharakan (grey receding hair, fine grey moustache), which the bible forbids.

fixes.correction: Show Padmini Amma ALONE in the doorway, with no other person anywhere in the frame. Remove the seated man at the low writing desk entirely, and frame her from inside the anteroom so the desk is behind the viewer and out of frame. Keep her exactly as drawn in v01: thick black hair coiled at the nape, gold ball earrings, gold bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape hitched for walking, barefoot, leaning on her long walking stick, with a wry half-smile, the sound that is not quite a laugh. Keep the dark wooden door frame and warm laterite wall. Outside the doorway: heavy, low, grey overcast sky, still palms, a DRY stone courtyard and no falling rain, because the rain has not yet fallen. Leave the plain laterite wall to her right clear and low-detail for two balloons.
fixes.issues: Padmini herself is excellent and on-sheet. But a bare-chested man with full long black hair in a low knot and a thick moustache sits at Ramayyan's writing desk with the stylus. He matches neither Ramayyan (receding hair, clean-shaven, plain white cloth) nor Nagoji (rust-red turban, tunic), and he reads as a bare-headed Nagoji double sitting in Ramayyan's place, which breaks continuity with 2.1 and 2.3. The doorway also shows a wet, misty courtyard, although page 1 says the rain has not yet fallen.

fixes.correction: Make this a head-and-shoulders CLOSE-UP of Nagoji's face filling the left two-thirds of the frame. His head is turning away from the doorway on the left toward Ramayyan on the right, his eyes sliding right. Keep the v01 rust-red turban, long curly black hair, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud and cream tunic with red sash, but give him a completely CLEAN-SHAVEN chin and jaw, with no stubble, stipple or beard shadow. At the lower right, show Ramayyan bowed over his palm leaf as in v01: receding hairline with curly black hair at the sides, clean-shaven, plain white cloth, his stylus moving on the leaf on the low dark wooden desk, beside a brass oil lamp with an open wick. Draw no soldiers or guards anywhere, in particular no tan or khaki tunics, cross-belts or uniform-like dress. Keep the warm laterite wall and dark wooden pillars, and leave the upper-right wall clear and low-detail for one caption.
fixes.issues: Three problems. (1) The framing is a three-quarter figure shot that repeats 2.1, not the script's close-up of 'Nagoji's face' turning from her to Ramayyan. (2) Nagoji's chin and jaw carry visible stippled stubble, but CONTINUITY requires a clean-shaven chin outside captivity. (3) Two background guards wear tan or khaki tunics with shoulder cross-straps and khaki turbans, which read as uniformed sepoys and contradict the chapter's Nair lock (bare-chested, short white mundu, front topknot, no coats or uniforms). Ramayyan and his desk are good.

fixes.correction: Keep v01's insert composition: Padmini's hand with its gold bangle holding the letter at centre, her other hand on the long walking stick at left against her cream gold-bordered sari, and the cord hanging loose from the end of the leaf with a small red-brown lac seal on the thread. Make the ola a THIN, slightly curved strip of dried palm leaf in pale straw colour, with a small hole near one end for the cord, not a thick wooden board; fine incised lines only, no dark rows of script-like marks. Show NO person in the background: remove the bearded, topknotted man at the desk. Behind the hand put only the laterite wall, dark wooden pillars and a brass oil lamp with an open wick, softly out of focus. Through the doorway: heavy, low, grey overcast sky and still palms as in 2.1 and 2.2, not blue sky with white clouds. Leave the upper-right wall and the top band clear and low-detail for two captions.
fixes.issues: The hand, stick, cord and lac seal work well, with no legible script and an unreadable seal. But a bearded, topknotted, bare-chested man sits at the writing desk in the background with his face visible. He is not Ramayyan, who sits at that desk in 2.1 and 2.3, so the room's continuity breaks. The ola is drawn as a thick wooden board, not a thin palm-leaf strip. The doorway shows bright blue sky with white clouds, while 2.1 and 2.2 are heavily overcast.

fixes.correction: Show Padmini Amma ALONE in the anteroom, with no other person in the frame. Remove the bearded man at the writing desk, keep the desk out of frame, and remove the two turbaned men in the doorway. Keep her as drawn in v01: thick black hair coiled at the nape, gold ball earrings, gold bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape, the long walking stick in one hand. Her other hand holds the palm-leaf letter LOWERED to waist height, while her eyes look away from it into the middle distance, her face still and thoughtful. The letter is a thin, pale, dried palm-leaf strip with fine incised lines only, no dark rows of script-like marks, its cord hanging loose with a small lac seal. Keep the warm laterite wall, dark wooden pillars and hanging brass oil lamp with open wicks. Through the doorway: heavy, low, grey overcast sky and a dry courtyard as in 2.1, with no rain. Leave the plain laterite wall to her right clear and low-detail for two balloons.
fixes.issues: Padmini is on-sheet, and her gaze to the middle distance is right. But a bearded, topknotted, bare-chested man sits at Ramayyan's writing desk and looks up at her, prominent and fully readable. He replaces Ramayyan from 2.1 and 2.3 with a different face. Two turbaned, moustached men stand in the doorway, and their dress matches neither Ramayyan, Nagoji nor the Nair lock (front topknot, short mundu). The leaf in her hand carries dense dark rows of script-like marks, which read as pseudo-text. The leaf is held at chest height rather than lowered.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition exactly: Padmini barefoot on the earth bund at left-centre, stick in her right hand, left arm extended pointing up and to the right at the pepper vines climbing the support trees, the terraced paddies and misty hills behind her at left, open grey sky in the upper left kept clear for lettering, and villagers working the vines at right. Change only two things. First, every village woman among the vines wears 1740s Kerala dress: a plain off-white or earth-toned mundu with a single cloth draped over one shoulder or tied above the chest, bare arms and shoulders, and NO stitched blouse, no sleeves and no fitted bodice of any colour. The two women at right must not wear red short-sleeved blouses. Second, the village headman standing beside Padmini must match the next panel: a man of about forty-five with a thick black moustache and a CLEAN-SHAVEN chin and jaw (no beard of any kind), a plain white head cloth tied as a band around his head, a white gold-striped towel hanging over both shoulders, a bare chest, a cream mundu with a narrow gold-striped border, and empty hands with no staff.
fixes.issues: v01 has a good composition and a correct Padmini: cream sari with a gold border, old drape with no blouse, black hair coiled at the nape, gold stud earrings and necklace, barefoot on the bund, stick in hand, pointing up at pepper vines on living support trees above terraced paddy. There is open sky at upper left for the caption and balloon. It fails on two counts. (1) Anachronism: the two village women working the vines at right, one of them large in the right foreground, wear stitched red short-sleeved blouses. In 1740s Travancore that is a 19th-century garment. A prior review in this project (ch9 4.3 servant) corrected the same fault. (2) Neighbour continuity: the headman here has a full grey-black beard, a gold-striped turban and a staff. In 3.2 (v01, acceptable) the headman has only a moustache, a clean chin, a plain white head-band and empty hands, so the reader sees two different headmen in consecutive panels. Regenerating 3.1 to match 3.2 fixes both.

fixes.correction: Keep this image exactly as it is: sunset light, the great jackfruit tree over the worn stone platform, the horse lines along the compound wall at left, the jar carriers, the women lighting lamps on the verandah, Padmini at left with her stick gesturing toward Nagoji, and Nagoji at right facing her with rust-red turban, tiny gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, red sash, sword and boots. Change one thing only. Nagoji's LEFT sleeve (the arm on the viewer's right, whose hand holds the scabbard) must come down to the wrist like his right sleeve: a full cream tunic sleeve covering the whole forearm to the wrist, with only the back of his hand showing below the cuff. No forearm skin, brand, scar, burn patch or mark may be visible on either arm.
fixes.issues: v01 gets almost everything right. It has a sunset estate yard with the great jackfruit tree over a stone platform, horse lines along the compound wall, jar carriers walking off, women lighting brass lamps along the verandah in the old drape, and the Nair house with its tiered tile roofs. Padmini (correct) and Nagoji face each other. Nagoji's face is correct: moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, rust turban, red sash, sword and boots. Failure: his LEFT sleeve is pushed up to the elbow, and his bare left forearm shows a large mottled pale scar patch on the outer, back-of-hand side. The prompt requires that in present scenes his sleeves stay down to the wrists. Even when the brand is shown, the bible puts it on the INNER forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, as a defined patch beside a thin white scar. This mark is on the wrong face of the arm and runs most of its length. It is also inconsistent with 3.3, where both sleeves are down. Minor, not the reason for rejection: the jar carriers read as grown men rather than boys, and the space for Nagoji's balloon beside his turban is tight.

fixes.correction: Keep this exact composition and nothing else changes: the wide overcast beach, horses walking in the shallow wash along the tide line, the long loose file receding to the left, and Nagoji at the head on the right in his rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers and boots, riding Kayal (ochre red-brown bay, black mane, tail and lower legs, no white markings). Change only the Madurai riders: EVERY Madurai rider wears a high-wrapped WHITE or off-white turban with a knee-length white jama and a plain cloth waistband. There is NO green turban anywhere in this panel (Raza Khan is not shown here). No rider except Nagoji wears an ear stud. The Maravar riders stay bare-headed with short curly hair, short dark jackets and hitched white mundus, on visibly smaller ponies whose backs are about a head lower than the tall dark Madurai horses. Keep the top third as open, low-detail overcast sky, clear of palm fronds and lance tips, for three caption boxes.
fixes.issues: v01 is otherwise strong: overcast light, hooves in the wash, a long file, Nagoji at the head on the right matching his sheet (curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, rust turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots), Kayal correct (ochre bay, black mane and lower legs, no white), Maravar riders bare-headed in short brown jackets and hitched mundus, and open sky for the three captions. It fails on one figure. The second-rank Madurai rider at about x 0.23 wears a deep GREEN turban. The bible says Raza Khan alone wears green, so readers will take him for Raza. But he has a full bushy black beard, a fuller face and a gold ear stud, not Raza's lean hawk face with a grey-streaked goatee and pointed moustache. Panel 4.5 on the same page draws Raza correctly, so the page would show two different Razas. If he is meant as an ordinary trooper instead, the bible bans green turbans in the Madurai troop. His head is about 11% of frame height, too big to ignore.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition: Nagoji at centre on Kayal (ochre red-brown bay, black mane and lower legs, no white markings) in his rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and boots, torso turned toward the riders, right arm extended with an open hand as he addresses them. The Madurai lancers are on the left, the Maravar riders on the right, and the overcast beach and sea stay as drawn. Fix two things. (1) EVERY Madurai rider wears a high-wrapped WHITE or off-white turban and a white jama. There is NO green turban anywhere in this panel (Raza Khan is not in it), and no rider except Nagoji wears an ear stud. (2) The Maravar riders match panel 4.1: bare-headed with short curly hair, each in a short dark short-sleeved jacket over the chest (not bare-chested), white mundus hitched to the knee, bare legs. They ride smaller ponies whose backs are about a head lower than the Madurai horses. Keep the upper-right sky open and low-detail for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: v01 gets the beat right: Nagoji on Kayal (correct, no white markings) turned with his right arm out in an open-handed address, white-turbaned Madurai lancers on the left, Maravar riders on the right, and open sky upper right. Two continuity failures. (1) The front Madurai rider at the top-left edge wears a GREEN turban and is again drawn with a full black beard and a gold ear stud. By the bible's green-turban rule he reads as Raza Khan, but his face does not match Raza's sheet or the correct Raza in 4.5. (2) The Maravar riders are bare-chested with only white shoulder cloths. The page notes, 4.1 and Ponnan in 4.2 and 4.3 all give them short dark jackets, so the same men change costume within the page.

fixes.correction: Keep Raza Khan exactly as drawn on his black Madurai horse, along with the beach, the surf and the overcast sky: deep green high-wrapped turban, lean face, hawk nose, pointed moustache, grey-streaked goatee, the puckered scar on his anatomical LEFT cheek (our right) turned toward camera in three-quarter view, right hand raised adjusting the turban. Fix three things. (1) Nagoji's mare Kayal has a plain ochre red-brown bay face with NO white star, blaze, stripe or snip anywhere, plus a black mane and black lower legs, exactly as on her sheet. (2) Move Nagoji to the far LEFT EDGE of the frame, his body and horse cropped by the panel border but his face (curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, rust-red turban) still inside the frame and turned toward Raza, so Raza is the clear subject filling the centre and right. (3) Any background riders are Madurai lancers in WHITE or off-white high-wrapped turbans and white jamas, with NO green turbans and no green sashes, since Raza alone wears green. Keep open, low-detail sky above both men's heads for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: Raza Khan himself is excellent and matches his sheet: deep green high-wrapped turban, lean hawk face, pointed moustache, grey-streaked goatee, and the scar on his anatomical LEFT cheek turned toward camera, with his right hand adjusting the turban. The panel fails on three points. (1) Nagoji's mount, Kayal, has a clear white star or blaze on her forehead. The script and bible say she has no white markings. (2) The background riders wear green turbans and green sashes. Raza alone wears green, and the Madurai troop is white-turbaned, as in 4.1 and 4.4. (3) Framing: Nagoji fills the left 40% as a co-lead instead of sitting at the edge of frame with Raza as the subject.

fixes.correction: Both of Nagoji's tunic sleeves stay down to the wrists, exactly as in the neighbouring panels: no rolled or pushed-back sleeve, no bare forearm, and no brand, burn, scar or mark visible on either arm or hand. His left hand rests on his knee with the cream sleeve covering the forearm to the wrist. Keep everything else that worked: the same laterite fort courtyard with the tiled gatehouse under cloudy daylight. Nagoji sits on the ground on the left in his rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar, with his thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and small gold ear stud. His head turns toward the older-faced Nair on the right, who is not laughing: bare-chested, front topknot, white mundu, matchlock held upright between his knees. Leave open cloudy sky above both men's heads for two balloons. Background Nair soldiers are bare-chested with front topknots, with no head cloths or turbans.
fixes.issues: Nagoji's face matches the sheet (turban, curled moustache, clean chin, ear stud), and the older Nair with the upright musket fits the beat. But Nagoji's LEFT sleeve is rolled to the elbow, and a pale scar and a puckered patch show on the top/outer side of his palm-down forearm, with the patch near the elbow. This breaks the bible (the brand belongs on the INNER forearm, a hand's width above the wrist). It is also inconsistent with 5.2 and 5.5, where both sleeves are down to the wrists, and the script does not call for the brand here. Minor: a background Nair wears a white head cloth.

fixes.correction: Frame this as a true close-up. Nagoji's head and the top of his shoulders fill most of the frame, his face large in the upper-middle and set slightly to one side. Keep clear, low-detail cloudy sky on the other side and above his turban for three stacked balloons. The courtyard behind him is soft and blurred: only vague shapes of laterite wall, tiled gatehouse roof and seated men, with no sharp detail. Any Nair soldiers visible behind him match the rest of the page: bare-chested, white mundu tied short, hair in a front topknot, no head cloths, headbands, turbans, shoulder cloths, tunics or beards. Keep what worked: rust-red turban, long curly black hair, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, red sash, the same cloudy daylight as the previous panels, and his hard, level gaze.
fixes.issues: Nagoji himself is on model (turban, curled moustache, clean chin, ear stud, sleeves to the wrists, sash, talwar). The panel misses the script framing, though. It is a waist-up medium shot, not close on his face, and the courtyard is sharp, not out of focus. The background soldiers also break the page's Nair look: many wear white headbands or turbans, toga-like white shoulder cloths or tunics, and beards. That is inconsistent with the bare-chested, bare-headed Nairs of 5.1 to 5.4.

fixes.correction: Marthanda Varma must match panel 6.1 and his V13 sheet: a man in his mid-thirties with JET-BLACK hair and no grey at all, the lean V13 face with strong cheekbones and a thick black curled moustache, bare-headed with his hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, bare-chested, a cream mundu with a gold border and gold necklaces. Mathoo Tharakan (grey receding hair, fine grey moustache, gold cross on his chest, white cloth with a gold border, standing) is the ONLY grey-haired man. Varma's index finger traces the inked coastline at the centre-left of the cloth map while his eyes turn up and sideways in a glance at Tharakan. Only these two at the table: no seated bearded man and no other figure at the frame edges, and any guards must be small and distant. Keep the lower-right quarter of the frame to plain table and map edge, with no lamp or bowl there, because a tight inset will be laid over it. Keep the open sky at upper right clear for two balloons. Use the same open tiled-roof war hall, overcast daylight (no sunset glow) and lines-only cloth map as panel 6.1.
fixes.issues: Varma is drawn with heavily grey-streaked hair and an older, heavier face. That does not match the V13 sheet or panel 6.1, where his hair is black, and it makes him read like a twin of the grey-haired Tharakan. No side knot is visible. He looks down at the map instead of glancing at Tharakan. An unscripted bearded man sits cross-legged at the left edge, where readers may take him for Ramayyan or a new character. The light changes to a sunset glow, unlike the overcast daylight of 6.1. A lamp and a bowl fill the lower right, where the 6.3 inset will sit.

fixes.correction: Make this a TIGHT close-up inset, not a figure shot: frame only the cloth map surface at hand height, with no faces, no bodies above the wrists and no sea or hall view. Ramayyan's thin brown fingers, with a fold of plain white cloth at the wrist, set ONE small plain copper coin (its face too small to read) on a mark on the inked coastline. Varma's bare brown index fingertip rests on the same coastline just beside it, entering from the opposite edge of the frame. Show exactly two hands, one each, each with five fingers. No bowl of coins and no other coins. The map is hand-drawn ink on cloth: coastline, rivers and hill marks as lines only, no lettering, with a pebble and a shell token nearby. Keep one corner of plain, low-detail cloth free for a caption.
fixes.issues: The script calls for a tight inset of fingers and coin. This is a medium figure shot of Ramayyan with a wide sea view, so it would not work as a small inset. The hands are wrong: two hands hold the bundle and stylus while a third places the coin. The palm-leaf bundle looks like a bundle of straw sticks. Ramayyan has slicked-back straight hair and a bare shoulder, unlike his curly side hair and full white wrap in 6.1 and 6.4. Varma's tracing finger is missing. A bowl of loose coins competes with the single Dutch coin.

fixes.correction: Marthanda Varma must match panel 6.1 and his V13 sheet: mid-thirties, JET-BLACK hair with no grey streaks, the lean V13 face with strong cheekbones and a thick black curled moustache, his hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, NO gold ear stud, bare-chested, a cream mundu with a gold border and gold necklaces. Mathoo Tharakan is the only grey-haired man: grey receding hair, fine grey moustache, gold cross on his chest, white cloth with a gold border. Draw them as two true side profiles facing each other across the cloth map, Tharakan on the left and Varma on the right, both bent slightly over the map, which is lines only with no lettering. No third person: no seated bearded man at the left edge and no figures at the table. Use the same open tiled-roof war hall and overcast daylight as panel 6.1. Keep the open sky in the upper middle, between and above their heads, clear for Tharakan's long balloon and Varma's reply.
fixes.issues: Varma again has grey-streaked hair and an older face, which does not match the V13 sheet or the black-haired Varma of 6.1. He also wears a round gold ear stud, which is Nagoji's identifier. The script asks for two profiles; this shows two three-quarter views. The same unscripted bearded man as in 6.2 sits at the left edge, this time with a sword, adding a third figure to a two-person panel.

fixes.correction: Reverse the direction of travel so the convoy visibly climbs AWAY from the sea. The red earth road rises from the lower-left foreground to the upper right, deeper into the forested hills. Every pair of yoked humped bullocks, every cart and every merchant faces and walks toward the upper right, uphill. The lead cart is highest on the road and the line trails back down toward the viewer. The empty sea, with no ships, lies behind them in the far left distance. Keep everything else: the misty forested ghat, heavy wooden carts piled with tied pepper sacks, Syrian Christian merchants in white mundus, shoulder cloths and white head cloths walking beside the wheels, the full-width strip format and the wide overcast sky across the top for the voice-over box.
fixes.issues: The direction of travel is reversed. Every ox pair and merchant faces left and walks downhill: the lead cart is lowest in the foreground and the line trails up the hill to the right. The convoy is heading toward the sea in the far left distance, when the beat is carts CLIMBING a ghat pass inland with the empty sea behind them, carrying pepper away from the blockaded harbours. Everything else works: forested ghat, pepper sacks, paired bullocks, Syrian Christian merchants in white walking beside the wheels, an empty sea with no ships, no text, and wide sky for the voice-over box.

fixes.correction: Keep the composition, the muted grey flashback palette, the burning roofs and smoke columns, the distant ships with small gun flashes and the open grey sky across the upper part. But there are NO European or blue-coated soldiers anywhere on land. In November the Dutch only bombarded from the sea and never came ashore, so no tricornes, blue coats, white cross-belts or European muskets appear among the people on the palm road, on the beach or in the town. The column streaming inland is only Colachel townsfolk (fisher families, women with bundles and baskets on their heads, children, a few bullock carts), with at most a few bare-chested Travancore Nair soldiers in white mundus tied short, with front topknots and matchlocks. The Dutch appear only as the distant ships offshore. No signature, monogram or scribble in any corner.
fixes.issues: Most of v01 works: the burning town, smoke columns, distant ships with small gun flashes, the refugee column on the palm road and an open grey sky for both captions. But at least four or five VOC soldiers in blue coats, tricornes and white cross-belts walk in the middle of the refugee column next to the bullock carts. That contradicts the beat: in November the Dutch only bombarded from the sea ('Three days, and then they sailed away'), and 7.2 is where they first land ('In February, they came back to stay'). There is also a faint scribble like a signature over the fence in the bottom-right corner.

fixes.correction: Keep the distant view from the rocky shore, the grey smoke drifting over the water, the burned palm-thatch houses, and the anchored ship with a single longboat pulling toward it, oars rising. Draw it in the same clean ink line and painted colour as the neighbouring panels, not a soft photographic painting. Tengapattanam is an undefended fishing village: no stone walls, bastions, fortress, castle, church tower or lighthouse anywhere on the shore or headland. The temple is a low Kerala temple with a sloping tiled roof that is visibly scorched and blackened, with smoke rising from it; never a European gabled building and never a tall tower. In the longboat, the small huddled shapes must clearly read as captive women in saris with their heads covered and small children pressed against them, with two or three rowers at the oars; no hoods, and no soldiers seated as passengers. Keep the open grey sky in the upper part clear for two lettering lines.
fixes.issues: v01 has the distant view, the smoke, the burned houses and a longboat rowing toward an anchored ship, but it fails on several points. (1) A long intact stone fortress wall with bastions runs along the beach, and a European castle or lighthouse-like tower stands on the headland. Neither is in the script, and an intact stone fort clashes with the half-built mud fort in 7.4. (2) The 'temple' is a tall gopuram fused onto a European gabled building, and its tiled roof looks intact, not scorched. (3) The figures in the longboat read as hooded adults or monks, not as captive women and children, so the slave-sale beat behind Ramayyan's lines is lost. (4) The rendering is soft and photographic, not the clean ink line of the neighbouring panels.

fixes.correction: Reframe as a true top-down overhead shot looking straight down onto the hand-drawn cloth map, with the map filling most of the frame and the dark wooden table edge showing only at the borders. Draw no heads, faces or bodies of any person anywhere in the panel: no standing or seated men, no bearded onlookers, no guards. The only figure is Varma's right hand and bare forearm with a gold bangle, entering from the lower-right edge. His fingertips sweep a short line of five or six dark river pebbles inland across the dashed inland-road line just behind the coast mark, closing the road. Turn the map so the sea side (pale blue-grey wash) runs along the top of the frame, filling the upper-left corner where the inset will sit. The coastline crosses the upper third, and the single small copper coin, its face too small to read, sits exactly on the coastline, not in the water. Keep the map as ink lines only (coast, rivers, small hill marks, the dashed road) with scattered pebble and shell tokens, no lettering, place names, grid or compass rose. Keep warm light from small brass open-wick lamps at the table edge. Leave the plain inland cloth in the lower-left and lower-centre of the map low-detail for three balloons.
fixes.issues: Rejected. The framing is wrong: the script asks for an overhead view on the cloth map, but v01 is an eye-level medium shot of Varma bending over the table. Readable unscripted men fill the panel. A bare-chested bearded man with a red waist sash and hand on chin stands upper left, a bearded seated courtier sits at the right, and two spear guards stand behind. Nagoji and Ramayyan both speak in this panel from off-frame, so readers would take these off-model men for them. The sea side of the map is at the lower left, so the 8.4 inset in the upper corner cannot sit over it. The coin sits in the water, not on the coast mark.

fixes.correction: Draw Varma alone, seen from Nagoji's point of view across the table. Varma stands upright behind the cloth map, turned square to the viewer, framed from the waist up. His level, direct gaze looks straight out of the panel. One hand rests flat on the map; the other hangs at his side, not pointing. Match his V13 sheet face: thick moustache, clean chin, pearl ear drops. His hair is fully black with no grey at all, tied in a knot (side knot above his LEFT ear). He is bare-headed and bare-chested, with gold bead necklaces and a cream mundu with a gold border. Draw no other person: no over-the-shoulder foreground figure, no Nagoji, no seated or standing courtiers, no bald man with forehead marks, no guards or bystanders. Keep the night war hall: timber pillars, a sloping tiled roof, the open side onto the dark moonlit sea with palms, and small brass open-wick lamps on the table. The map edge shows ink lines only, with no lettering. Leave the dark night sky and roof band on both sides of his head clear for three balloons.
fixes.issues: Rejected. The man Varma addresses, in the right foreground (over the shoulder, presumably Nagoji), is off-model: bearded, no rust-red turban, a large hanging gold earring, and a maroon cloth over white. Varma himself has grey-streaked hair worn loose, not black hair in a knot, which reads as the older figure from his sheet. The panel is crowded with unscripted readable men: a standing bearded man with arms crossed, a bald man with forehead marks who could be mistaken for Ramayyan, a seated grey-bearded courtier, and two bearded guards. The beat (Varma turned full on Nagoji, direct and level) gets lost, and the page's cast becomes confused.

fixes.correction: Keep the wide bottom-strip composition. Nagoji stands on the left: rust-red turban, cream tunic with the sleeves down, broad red sash, talwar, leaning over the table with one finger near the copper coin. Varma stands on the right: bare-headed, bare-chested, gold bead necklaces, cream mundu with a gold border, both hands on the table. The two face each other in profile across the cloth map, with the small copper coin on the coastline between them. Remove the seated man at the centre back of the table and every other person: no seated courtier, no guards. In particular, draw no background men in red turbans or red sashes. Behind the two men, show only the hall's timber pillars, the laterite half-wall, the dark open sea and palms under a night sky. Draw no ships, harbour, quay, fort walls or lit windows. Nagoji's chin and jaw are clean-shaven and smooth with no stubble, and he wears a tiny flush gold ear stud. Varma's hair is fully black. Keep the map as ink lines only with no lettering, and keep the small brass open-wick lamps. Leave the roof band at the top-left corner and the night-sky band between and above their heads low-detail for a caption and two balloons.
fixes.issues: Rejected. The two principals and the coin between them are right: Nagoji points at the coin and Varma leans on the table. But a sharply drawn seated man in white cloth sits at the centre back of the table, the spot Ramayyan holds in 8.1. He has a thick moustache and full black hair, so he reads as an off-model Ramayyan in the middle of the strip. Four background guards wear rust-red turbans, white tunics and red sashes, so they read as copies of Nagoji's commander dress, while the other panels' guards are bare-chested Nairs. Ships with lit windows sit at a quay by a fort just outside the hall, unlike the open dark sea in 8.1 to 8.5. Nagoji also shows light stubble on his chin and jaw.

fixes.correction: Keep this wide night composition: the jackfruit tree with its low stone platform, the tiled estate house behind, the horse lines with heads hanging low and the riders asleep on woven mats on the right, the small brass oil lamp with an open wick and no glass chimney on the ground between the two men, and both men's costumes exactly as drawn. Fix posture and eyelines to match the panels before and after. Neither man squats or crouches. Dhanaji (short black beard, white Maratha pagdi turban, indigo quilted tunic, no sash) sits on the left on the same low wooden stool as in the earlier panel. His bare talwar lies across his knees with the whetstone still in one hand. He has just lifted his head from the blade and turned it toward Nagoji, eyebrows raised, mouth slightly open, eyes on Nagoji's face and not on the sky or the tree. Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, boots, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud) sits on a low stone ledge on the right with his talwar across his knees, head bowed, gazing at the lamp flame and not at Dhanaji. Make both men small in the frame, each about a third of the frame height, and leave the dark sky in the upper right open and empty. The sleeping riders lie on their sides under blankets with their heads on rolled cloth, clearly asleep and not face-down.
fixes.issues: The only candidate (v01) breaks continuity with the panels on either side and misplays Dhanaji's beat. Both men are crouched on their heels on bare ground and Dhanaji's stool has gone. His talwar is sheathed at his hip, although 10.4 shows him sharpening it and 11.1 has the blade across his knees. He gazes up into the tree canopy above and past Nagoji, so his surprise reads as a reaction to something overhead, not to Nagoji's words. The two men are also fairly large for a 'small under the tree' wide shot. The identities are correct (Nagoji has a clean chin and the ear stud, Dhanaji the white pagdi and indigo tunic). The setting is right: the brass open-wick lamp between them, horse lines with heads low, and sleeping riders on mats.

fixes.correction: Nagoji's cream tunic sleeves are pulled DOWN TO HIS WRISTS on both arms, as in panels 11.3 and 11.5. No bare forearms, and no brand, scar, tattoo, blotch, dirt mark or any other marking on either forearm or the backs of his hands. Keep everything else exactly as it was. Padmini stands at left in the cream old-Kerala drape with gold border and no blouse, black hair coiled at the nape, gold necklace and ear studs, and her long wooden walking stick planted on the damp, lamp-reflecting earth; she looks down at Nagoji. Nagoji sits on the low stone ledge under the jackfruit tree at right, looking up at her: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, red sash, talwar at his hip, cream trousers, boots, hands loosely clasped over his knees. The small brass oil lamp with an open wick sits on the ground between them, the horse lines are in the background, and the dark sky and foliage at upper centre stay clear for lettering.
fixes.issues: Nagoji's sleeves are pushed up to the elbows, unlike 11.3 and 11.5 where they reach the wrists. A mottled brand-like patch is painted on the OUTER (top) surface of his left forearm near the elbow, visible at full size. The bible places the brand on the INNER left forearm a hand's width above the wrist, with the white scar beside it, and earlier rows forbid it on the outer forearm. The script does not call for the brand in this beat. Everything else works: Padmini on her sheet (cream Kerala drape, gold border, coiled hair, gold necklace, stick on wet earth, looking down at him), and Nagoji seated with a clean chin, moustache, stud and boots. The lamp, the tree and the lettering space are also fine.

fixes.correction: Nagoji MUST wear his rust-red wrapped turban exactly as on his commander sheet. It covers the crown of his head, with his long curly black hair showing only below it at the sides and nape. He is never bare-headed in this panel. Keep everything else from the previous attempt. Padmini kneels in her cream sari with its narrow gold border, shoulders bare in the old Kerala drape, black hair coiled at the nape, palms joined and head bowed before the stone serpents, her wooden walking stick upright beside her. Nagoji stands a pace behind her, barefoot on the leaf litter, in a cream long-sleeved tunic, red sash and cream trousers, with the sheathed talwar at his hip and his hands folded in front. He has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud. The lamp-lit serpent idols, termite mounds and roots sit under the massive tree on the right, and the dark night area at upper centre stays clear of detail for the balloon. No text or letters anywhere.
fixes.issues: Nagoji is bare-headed, with his long curly hair loose and no turban. Script 12.3 says 'turban and talwar kept', and the chapter 13 bible row puts him in the rust-red turban. Everything else works: Padmini kneeling with palms joined and head bowed before the idols, her walking stick beside her; Nagoji barefoot, with moustache, clean chin, ear stud, cream tunic, red sash and sheathed talwar.

fixes.correction: Compose this small inset as a view looking OUT of the grove, away from the shrine: no serpent idol, no serpent stones, no shrine lamp and no lit foreground anywhere in the frame. Fill the frame with tall black tree-trunk silhouettes in the near and middle distance against a deep blue-black night sky, with a gap between the trunks near the centre. Through that gap, far off and small but clearly the focal point, place a dim tiled-roof Kerala house with ONE single warm point of oil-lamp light at its doorway. That light is the only light in the picture. Keep the dark trunks, the dark foliage and the far house that worked in the upper right of the previous version. Leave a plain dark patch of sky at upper left for the off-panel balloon. No people, no text.
fixes.issues: The script beat is lost. The frame centres on a large lit cobra idol, the serpent stones and the shrine's own oil lamp, which is the brightest point. The distant house with its lamplight is a tiny detail at the top right (about x 0.8-0.87, y 0.2-0.26), and at inset size it would be unreadable or under the Dhanaji balloon. There are also two light sources, not the single point of lamplight the script asks for.

fixes.correction: Nagoji is seen from behind over his shoulder in the right foreground and must match his chapter look. He wears the rust-red turban (seen from behind, it covers his crown, with long curly black hair falling from under it to his shoulders), a cream tunic and the broad red sash over his shoulder, and a small gold stud in the visible ear. Any visible sliver of his cheek and jaw is smooth and CLEAN-SHAVEN with no stubble or beard; only the tip of the thick curled moustache may show. No beige shawl, never bare-headed. Keep Revathi exactly as before: dry cheeks, a sad knowing smile, blue-and-gold sari, coin necklace, jasmine braid and gold armlet, with the lamp-lit serpent grove behind her. Keep the dark space above her head for two balloons. Keep both figures low, as in the neighbouring panels: Nagoji seated on the leaf litter, Revathi kneeling close to him.
fixes.issues: The over-the-shoulder figure meant to be Nagoji is off model. He is bare-headed with loose curls (no rust-red turban), has a stubbled, bearded jaw (his chin must be clean-shaven) and wears a beige shawl instead of the cream tunic and red sash. He reads as a different man. Revathi is good: dry cheeks, a sad knowing smile, and her sari, coin necklace, jasmine braid and armlet all correct.

fixes.correction: The hand in the foreground touching the stone serpent must be REVATHI'S, not Nagoji's. Show her bare brown forearm with gold bangles reaching into the near foreground, her fingertips lightly brushing the carved coils of a moss-covered stone serpent close to the viewer, large and clearly lit by the small brass lamp. Put the serpent stone on the same side of the strip as Revathi, so her own arm reaches it naturally. Nagoji's hands stay away from the stone, resting on his knee. Beyond the hand, keep the pairing that worked: Revathi kneeling close behind Nagoji, her face at his ear, eyes lowered. Nagoji sits on the ground in the rust-red turban, cream tunic and broad red sash, with a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud. Keep the blue-black night and the serpent grove, and leave dark open space at upper left above the stones for the whisper balloon. No text.
fixes.issues: The key foreground action belongs to the wrong person. The hand touching the stone serpent's coils is Nagoji's (cream sleeve, reaching right), not Revathi's. Revathi's hand rests on his thigh instead. The rest works: Revathi is close behind him with her face at his ear and eyes lowered, and Nagoji has the turban, moustache, clean chin and ear stud.

fixes.correction: Keep the three diagonal slivers and keep the first two as drawn: the bandaged hands and the iron bar across the chained ankles, and the rope tearing through bandaged palms with its frayed free end whipping loose while young Keshavrao (short hacked hair, faint moustache, grey-brown rags) sinks with his ankles chained in a pair, no rope near him. In the first sliver, make the damp stone wall behind the hands visibly curved, like the inside of a vaulted cellar. In the third sliver, Revathi's face in the smoke is bare-headed, with her sari NOT drawn over her head. Her hair is in its long braid with jasmine and there is a thin pale cream sandalwood line at her hairline. Draw NO red vermilion in her hair parting and NO red mark on her forehead, because she is a widow. Keep her flat-coin necklace, gold bell earrings and the sorrowful smile. Below her, the horses pounding across the wet sand carry Madurai cavalry in white knee-length jama tunics and high-wrapped white or off-white turbans, seen from behind or at a distance. No rider wears a rust-red or red turban or a red sash, and no rider resembles Nagoji. Keep the blue-coated VOC soldiers in black tricornes firing through white smoke, the fort behind them and the plain, unmarked blue flags.
fixes.issues: Third sliver: Revathi has a red vermilion line in her hair parting and a red stroke on her forehead, which mark a married woman, but she is a widow in ch13. Her sari is also drawn over her head, which is off her sheet. The lead rider is a Nagoji double: rust-red turban, red sash and curled moustache, but black jackboots, a chest strap and a dark brown horse that is not Kayal. The cast override deliberately leaves Nagoji out of this panel. Background riders wear rust or pink turbans, against the Madurai troop rule. First sliver: the cellar wall is straight blocks, not curved. Slivers 1 and 2 otherwise work well: ankle bar, rope tearing through bandaged palms with its free end loose, and Keshavrao sinking chained with no rope near him.

fixes.correction: Keep the composition that worked: the jackfruit tree with fruit at left, the tiled estate house, the churned and hoofprinted mud, the grey-blue pre-dawn light, and the far fort wall on the right with tiny drummer silhouettes. Keep Kayal in the foreground (bay mare, ochre red-brown coat, black mane, tail and lower legs, quilted ochre saddle pad) beside Nagoji as he buckles on his talwar. Nagoji is the ONLY man in a rust-red turban and a red sash. The other men in the yard are Madurai troopers in knee-length white jama tunics with plain white cloth waistbands, loose trousers and high-wrapped white or off-white turbans (never red, rust or green), plus one or two bare-headed Maravar riders in short dark jackets with white mundus hitched. Show the drums arriving: two or three of these men have paused mid-saddling and turned their heads toward the distant fort wall on the right. Pull the camera back slightly so that Nagoji's brown laced riding boots show on his feet. Keep the open sky above the treeline at upper right low-detail for the captions, and keep the drummers clear of it.
fixes.issues: Two background men wear rust-red turbans and red sashes over cream tunics, which is Nagoji's own costume. A third has a red sash. This breaks the bible's Madurai troop look (white or off-white turbans, never red or rust, plain waistbands) and clashes with the white-turbaned riders in 4.1 and 10.5. On a full-width closing panel, readers cannot tell at a glance which man is Nagoji. The script beat of men turning their heads toward the drums is missing: every man is busy with his horse. Nagoji's boots are cropped out of frame. What works: the jackfruit tree and estate house match 10.5. Kayal is on model (bay, black points, quilted ochre pad). Nagoji is buckling on his talwar on model. There are churned hoofprints and the far fort wall has tiny drummer silhouettes.
